0157: INVALID: Deligne gives |lambda_f(n)|²≤n^{2epsilon}, but multiplying this inequality by chi(n) is impermissible when chi(n)=-1, and Pólya–Vinogradov controls only unweighted character sums, not the arbitrarily weighted sum here. Equality f(n)=f′(n) merely forces lambda_f(n)=0 where chi(n)≠1; it does not make chi(n) nonnegative. Thus the displayed upper bound is unjustified.
0158: Invalid independently: the assertion that chi(n) is nonnegative for every n≤X is false, so the bound for X and hence Lemma 1 and Theorem 1.1 do not follow. It also suppresses the previously obtained N^epsilon dependence without establishing a uniform relation between N and q in the lemma as stated.
0159: At additive primes the conductor exponent is at least two, so N_0²≤N (up to the noted small-prime qualifications) supports the claimed exponent only if Theorem 1.1 had been proved; it was not.
